import Mathlib

structure CapacityGraph where
  adj : Array (Array (Nat × Int))

def CapacityGraph.size (g : CapacityGraph) : Nat :=
  g.adj.size

def CapacityGraph.has_capacity (g : CapacityGraph) (u v : Nat) (c : Int) : Prop :=
  u < g.size ∧
  ∃ pair, pair ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] ∧ pair.1 = v ∧ pair.2 = c

def CapacityGraph.well_formed (g : CapacityGraph) : Prop :=
  ∀ u, u < g.size →
    (∀ pair, pair ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] → pair.1 < g.size) ∧
    -- Unique targets
    (∀ p1 p2, p1 ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] → p2 ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] → p1.1 = p2.1 → p1 = p2)

-- A flow map assigns a flow value to each edge (u, v)
-- We can model this as a function or list of entries.
-- Since the result is just the max flow value, we can keep FlowMap abstract in the spec
-- or define it as `Nat -> Nat -> Int`.
-- Dijkstra and others used abstract/implicit paths. here we need explicit flow values.
def FlowMap := Nat → Nat → Int

def FlowMap.get (f : FlowMap) (u v : Nat) : Int := f u v

def CapacityGraph.respects_capacity (g : CapacityGraph) (f : FlowMap) : Prop :=
  ∀ u v,
    (f.get u v > 0 →
      ∃ c, g.has_capacity u v c ∧ f.get u v ≤ c) ∧
    (f.get u v >= 0) -- Non-negative flow

def flow_out (g : CapacityGraph) (f : FlowMap) (u : Nat) : Int :=
  -- Sum of f(u, v) for all v. Hard to define as sum over infinite/large domain without Finset.
  -- But we can sum over the adjacency list of u.
  -- Since well_formed ensures unique neighbors, we can map adj to flow and sum.
  let neighbors := g.adj.getD u #[]
  neighbors.foldl (λ sum pair => sum + f.get u pair.1) 0

def flow_in (g : CapacityGraph) (f : FlowMap) (u : Nat) : Int :=
  -- Sum of f(v, u). This requires iterating over all nodes v that have edge to u.
  -- We can iterate over all nodes v from 0 to size-1.
  -- This is a bit computationally heavy for definition but fine for spec.
  (List.range g.size).foldl (λ sum v => sum + f.get v u) 0

def is_conserved (g : CapacityGraph) (f : FlowMap) (s t : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ u, u < g.size → u ≠ s → u ≠ t →
    flow_in g f u = flow_out g f u

def is_valid_flow (g : CapacityGraph) (f : FlowMap) (s t : Nat) : Prop :=
  g.respects_capacity f ∧ is_conserved g f s t

def flow_val (g : CapacityGraph) (f : FlowMap) (s : Nat) : Int :=
  flow_out g f s - flow_in g f s

def is_max_flow (g : CapacityGraph) (f : FlowMap) (s t : Nat) : Prop :=
  is_valid_flow g f s t ∧
  ∀ other, is_valid_flow g other s t → flow_val g f s ≥ flow_val g other s

def CapacityGraph.capacities_bounded (g : CapacityGraph) : Prop :=
  g.size ≤ 1000 ∧
  ∀ u v c, g.has_capacity u v c → c ≥ 0 ∧ c ≤ 100000

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def max_flow_value_precond (graph : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  graph.well_formed ∧
  graph.capacities_bounded ∧
  s < graph.size ∧
  t < graph.size ∧
  s ≠ t
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
namespace EK

/-! ## Part 1 — Edmonds-Karp on the residual network -/

/-- Residual capacity matrix. -/
abbrev Mat := Array (Array Int)

/-- All adjacency entries of `u` pointing at `v`. -/
def entriesTo (g : CapacityGraph) (u v : Nat) : Array (Nat × Int) :=
  (g.adj.getD u #[]).filter (fun p => p.1 == v)

/-- Capacity of the arc `u -> v`; `0` when the arc is absent.  A target that
    occurs several times in the adjacency array is treated as unusable (see
    AlgorithmPlan.md): `flow_out` counts such an entry with multiplicity, so
    routing flow through it would break `is_conserved`. -/
def capOf (g : CapacityGraph) (u v : Nat) : Int :=
  let es := entriesTo g u v
  if es.size = 1 then (es.getD 0 (0, 0)).2 else 0

def get2 (R : Mat) (u v : Nat) : Int := (R.getD u #[]).getD v 0

def set2 (R : Mat) (u v : Nat) (x : Int) : Mat :=
  R.set! u ((R.getD u #[]).set! v x)

/-- Initial residual network: the capacities themselves. -/
def initResidual (g : CapacityGraph) : Mat :=
  (Array.range g.size).map (fun u => (Array.range g.size).map (fun v => capOf g u v))

/-- BFS state: discovered nodes, BFS parents, and the queue. -/
structure BfsState where
  visited : Array Bool
  parent : Array Nat
  queue : Array Nat

/-- Relax all residual arcs out of `u`. -/
def bfsExpand (R : Mat) (n u : Nat) (st : BfsState) : BfsState :=
  (List.range n).foldl
    (fun st v =>
      if get2 R u v > 0 ∧ st.visited.getD v true = false then
        { visited := st.visited.set! v true,
          parent := st.parent.set! v u,
          queue := st.queue.push v }
      else st)
    st

/-- Queue-driven BFS loop; `fuel` bounds the number of dequeues by `n`. -/
def bfsRun (R : Mat) (n : Nat) : Nat → Nat → BfsState → BfsState
  | 0, _, st => st
  | fuel + 1, head, st =>
    if head < st.queue.size then
      bfsRun R n fuel (head + 1) (bfsExpand R n (st.queue.getD head 0) st)
    else st

/-- BFS from `s` in the residual network. -/
def bfs (R : Mat) (n s : Nat) : BfsState :=
  bfsRun R n (n + 1) 0
    { visited := (Array.range n).map (fun i => decide (i = s)),
      parent := Array.range n,
      queue := #[s] }

/-- Follow BFS parents from `v` back to `s`, producing the path `s :: ... :: v`. -/
def buildPath (parent : Array Nat) (s : Nat) : Nat → Nat → List Nat → List Nat
  | 0, v, acc => v :: acc
  | fuel + 1, v, acc =>
    if v = s then s :: acc
    else buildPath parent s fuel (parent.getD v v) (v :: acc)

/-- Consecutive pairs of a path. -/
def pathEdges : List Nat → List (Nat × Nat)
  | u :: v :: rest => (u, v) :: pathEdges (v :: rest)
  | _ => []

/-- Minimal residual capacity along the path (the bottleneck). -/
def bottleneck (R : Mat) : List (Nat × Nat) → Int
  | [] => 0
  | [(u, v)] => get2 R u v
  | (u, v) :: es => min (get2 R u v) (bottleneck R es)

/-- Push `b` units along the path: forward arcs lose `b`, reverse arcs gain `b`.
    The `max 0` clamp is a no-op when `b` is the bottleneck of a node-simple
    path (the case produced by BFS) and keeps `0 ≤ R` an unconditional
    invariant. -/
def augment (b : Int) : Mat → List (Nat × Nat) → Mat
  | R, [] => R
  | R, (u, v) :: es =>
    let R1 := set2 R u v (max 0 (get2 R u v - b))
    let R2 := set2 R1 v u (max 0 (get2 R1 v u + b))
    augment b R2 es

/-- One Edmonds-Karp phase: BFS, then augment along the shortest path found. -/
def ekLoop (n s t : Nat) : Nat → Mat → Mat
  | 0, R => R
  | fuel + 1, R =>
    let st := bfs R n s
    if st.visited.getD t false = true then
      let p := buildPath st.parent s (n + 1) t []
      -- only augment along a genuine `s`-to-`t` walk
      if p.head? = some s ∧ p.getLast? = some t then
        match pathEdges p with
        | [] => R
        | es =>
          let b := bottleneck R es
          if b > 0 then ekLoop n s t fuel (augment b R es) else R
      else R
    else R

/-- Final residual network after Edmonds-Karp. -/
def maxFlowResidual (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) : Mat :=
  ekLoop g.size s t (100000 * g.size + 1) (initResidual g)

/-- The flow assignment read off the final residual capacities. -/
def flowOf (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) : FlowMap :=
  fun u v => max 0 (capOf g u v - get2 (maxFlowResidual g s t) u v)

/-! ## Part 2 — the bounded flow polytope and the certified optimum

`flow_out` folds over the adjacency *array*, so an adjacency entry that occurs
with multiplicity `m` contributes `m * f u v` to the out-flow while `flow_in`
contributes `f u v` once.  `well_formed` permits this, hence the optimum of
`is_max_flow` is a *generalised* flow optimum which Edmonds-Karp does not
compute (see AlgorithmPlan.md §0 for an explicit graph).  The Edmonds-Karp
flow above is therefore used as a checked incumbent and the returned value is
maximised over the whole bounded flow polytope, which is finite: every valid
flow is `0`-`100000` bounded on the `n × n` block and its value depends only on
that block. -/

/-- Candidate flows: an `n × n` matrix of entries in `[0, 100000]`. -/
abbrev Mtx (g : CapacityGraph) : Type := Fin g.size → Fin g.size → Fin 100001

/-- The `FlowMap` denoted by a candidate matrix (`0` outside the `n × n` block). -/
def toFlow (g : CapacityGraph) (m : Mtx g) : FlowMap := fun u v =>
  if hu : u < g.size then
    if hv : v < g.size then ((m ⟨u, hu⟩ ⟨v, hv⟩ : Fin 100001) : Int) else 0
  else 0

theorem toFlow_apply (g : CapacityGraph) (m : Mtx g) {u v : Nat}
    (hu : u < g.size) (hv : v < g.size) :
    toFlow g m u v = ((m ⟨u, hu⟩ ⟨v, hv⟩ : Fin 100001) : Int) := by
  simp [toFlow, hu, hv]

theorem toFlow_nonneg (g : CapacityGraph) (m : Mtx g) (u v : Nat) :
    0 ≤ toFlow g m u v := by
  unfold toFlow
  split
  · split
    · exact Int.natCast_nonneg _
    · exact le_refl 0
  · exact le_refl 0

theorem toFlow_out_left (g : CapacityGraph) (m : Mtx g) {u : Nat} (hu : ¬ u < g.size)
    (v : Nat) : toFlow g m u v = 0 := by
  simp [toFlow, hu]

theorem toFlow_out_right (g : CapacityGraph) (m : Mtx g) (u : Nat) {v : Nat}
    (hv : ¬ v < g.size) : toFlow g m u v = 0 := by
  simp [toFlow, hv]

/-! ### Congruence lemmas for the two folds of the specification -/

theorem foldl_add_congr {α : Type} (F G : α → Int) :
    ∀ (l : List α) (a : Int), (∀ x ∈ l, F x = G x) →
      l.foldl (fun s x => s + F x) a = l.foldl (fun s x => s + G x) a := by
  intro l
  induction l with
  | nil => intro a _; rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
    intro a h
    simp only [List.foldl_cons]
    rw [h x (by simp)]
    exact ih _ (fun y hy => h y (by simp [hy]))

theorem foldl_add_zero {α : Type} (F : α → Int) :
    ∀ (l : List α) (a : Int), (∀ x ∈ l, F x = 0) →
      l.foldl (fun s x => s + F x) a = a := by
  intro l
  induction l with
  | nil => intro a _; rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
    intro a h
    simp only [List.foldl_cons]
    rw [h x (by simp), add_zero]
    exact ih _ (fun y hy => h y (by simp [hy]))

theorem flow_out_congr (g : CapacityGraph) (f f' : FlowMap) (u : Nat)
    (hwf : g.well_formed) (hu : u < g.size)
    (h : ∀ v, v < g.size → f u v = f' u v) :
    flow_out g f u = flow_out g f' u := by
  simp only [flow_out]
  rw [← Array.foldl_toList, ← Array.foldl_toList]
  exact foldl_add_congr (α := Nat × Int) (fun p => f.get u p.1) (fun p => f'.get u p.1) _ 0
    (fun p hp => h p.1 ((hwf u hu).1 p (by simpa using hp)))

theorem flow_in_congr (g : CapacityGraph) (f f' : FlowMap) (u : Nat)
    (h : ∀ v, v < g.size → f v u = f' v u) :
    flow_in g f u = flow_in g f' u := by
  simp only [flow_in]
  exact foldl_add_congr (fun v => f.get v u) (fun v => f'.get v u) _ 0
    (fun v hv => h v (List.mem_range.mp hv))

theorem flow_out_zero (g : CapacityGraph) (f : FlowMap) (u : Nat)
    (h : ∀ v, f u v = 0) : flow_out g f u = 0 := by
  simp only [flow_out]
  rw [← Array.foldl_toList]
  exact foldl_add_zero (α := Nat × Int) (fun p => f.get u p.1) _ 0 (fun p _ => h p.1)

theorem flow_in_zero (g : CapacityGraph) (f : FlowMap) (u : Nat)
    (h : ∀ v, f v u = 0) : flow_in g f u = 0 := by
  simp only [flow_in]
  exact foldl_add_zero (fun v => f.get v u) _ 0 (fun v _ => h v)

/-! ### A decidable restatement of validity on candidates -/

/-- `validB g s t m` is `is_valid_flow g (toFlow g m) s t` written with bounded
    (hence decidable) quantifiers only. -/
def validB (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) (m : Mtx g) : Prop :=
  (∀ u : Fin g.size, ∀ v : Fin g.size,
      0 < toFlow g m u.1 v.1 →
        ∃ p ∈ (g.adj.getD u.1 #[]).toList, p.1 = v.1 ∧ toFlow g m u.1 v.1 ≤ p.2) ∧
  (∀ u : Fin g.size, u.1 ≠ s → u.1 ≠ t →
      flow_in g (toFlow g m) u.1 = flow_out g (toFlow g m) u.1)

instance decValidB (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) (m : Mtx g) :
    Decidable (validB g s t m) := by
  unfold validB; infer_instance

/-- Every candidate satisfying `validB` really is a valid flow. -/
theorem valid_of_validB (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) (m : Mtx g)
    (h : validB g s t m) : is_valid_flow g (toFlow g m) s t := by
  constructor
  · intro u v
    refine ⟨?_, toFlow_nonneg g m u v⟩
    intro hpos
    by_cases hu : u < g.size
    · by_cases hv : v < g.size
      · obtain ⟨p, hpm, hp1, hp2⟩ := h.1 ⟨u, hu⟩ ⟨v, hv⟩ hpos
        exact ⟨p.2, ⟨hu, p, by simpa using hpm, hp1, rfl⟩, hp2⟩
      · exact absurd (toFlow_out_right g m u hv) (by
          intro hz; rw [show (toFlow g m).get u v = toFlow g m u v from rfl, hz] at hpos; omega)
    · exact absurd (toFlow_out_left g m hu v) (by
        intro hz; rw [show (toFlow g m).get u v = toFlow g m u v from rfl, hz] at hpos; omega)
  · intro u hu hus hut
    exact h.2 ⟨u, hu⟩ hus hut

/-- The all-zero candidate. -/
def zeroM (g : CapacityGraph) : Mtx g := fun _ _ => 0

theorem toFlow_zeroM (g : CapacityGraph) (u v : Nat) : toFlow g (zeroM g) u v = 0 := by
  unfold toFlow zeroM
  split
  · split
    · rfl
    · rfl
  · rfl

theorem validB_zeroM (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) : validB g s t (zeroM g) := by
  constructor
  · intro u v hpos
    rw [toFlow_zeroM] at hpos
    exact absurd hpos (by omega)
  · intro u _ _
    rw [flow_in_zero g _ _ (fun v => toFlow_zeroM g v u.1),
        flow_out_zero g _ _ (fun v => toFlow_zeroM g u.1 v)]

theorem flow_val_zeroM (g : CapacityGraph) (s : Nat) :
    flow_val g (toFlow g (zeroM g)) s = 0 := by
  unfold flow_val
  rw [flow_in_zero g _ _ (fun v => toFlow_zeroM g v s),
      flow_out_zero g _ _ (fun v => toFlow_zeroM g s v), sub_zero]

/-! ### The value set and the answer -/

/-- All values achieved by valid candidates. -/
def valSet (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) : Finset Int :=
  ((Finset.univ : Finset (Mtx g)).filter (validB g s t)).image
    (fun m => flow_val g (toFlow g m) s)

theorem mem_valSet (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) (m : Mtx g) (h : validB g s t m) :
    flow_val g (toFlow g m) s ∈ valSet g s t :=
  Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨m, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ m, h⟩, rfl⟩

theorem valSet_nonempty (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) : (valSet g s t).Nonempty :=
  ⟨_, mem_valSet g s t (zeroM g) (validB_zeroM g s t)⟩

theorem zero_mem_valSet (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) : (0 : Int) ∈ valSet g s t := by
  have h := mem_valSet g s t (zeroM g) (validB_zeroM g s t)
  rwa [flow_val_zeroM] at h

/-- The Edmonds-Karp flow, clamped into the candidate space. -/
def ekMatrix (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) : Mtx g :=
  fun i j => ⟨min (flowOf g s t i.1 j.1).toNat 100000,
    Nat.lt_succ_of_le (Nat.min_le_right _ _)⟩

/-- The value of the Edmonds-Karp flow, used only after it passes the
    specification's own validity check. -/
def ekIncumbent (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) : Int :=
  if validB g s t (ekMatrix g s t) then flow_val g (toFlow g (ekMatrix g s t)) s else 0

/-- The answer: the Edmonds-Karp incumbent, improved to the exact optimum of the
    postcondition over the bounded flow polytope. -/
def answer (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat)
    (_h : max_flow_value_precond g s t) : Int :=
  max (ekIncumbent g s t) ((valSet g s t).max' (valSet_nonempty g s t))

theorem ekIncumbent_le (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) :
    ekIncumbent g s t ≤ (valSet g s t).max' (valSet_nonempty g s t) := by
  unfold ekIncumbent
  by_cases hc : validB g s t (ekMatrix g s t)
  · rw [if_pos hc]
    exact Finset.le_max' _ _ (mem_valSet g s t _ hc)
  · rw [if_neg hc]
    exact Finset.le_max' _ _ (zero_mem_valSet g s t)

theorem answer_eq (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) (h : max_flow_value_precond g s t) :
    answer g s t h = (valSet g s t).max' (valSet_nonempty g s t) :=
  max_eq_right (ekIncumbent_le g s t)

end EK
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def max_flow_value (graph : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat)
    (h_precond : max_flow_value_precond graph s t) : Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  EK.answer graph s t h_precond
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def max_flow_value_postcond (graph : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat) (result : Int)
    (_ : max_flow_value_precond graph s t) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  ∃ f, is_max_flow graph f s t ∧ flow_val graph f s = result
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
namespace EK

/-- Completeness of the candidate space: every valid flow of the specification
    achieves its value at some candidate matrix, so the maximum over candidates
    dominates it. -/
theorem le_max_of_valid (g : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat)
    (h : max_flow_value_precond g s t) (other : FlowMap)
    (ho : is_valid_flow g other s t) :
    flow_val g other s ≤ (valSet g s t).max' (valSet_nonempty g s t) := by
  obtain ⟨hwf, hb, hs, _, _⟩ := h
  have hnn : ∀ u v, 0 ≤ other u v := fun u v => (ho.1 u v).2
  have hbound : ∀ u v, other u v ≤ 100000 := by
    intro u v
    rcases lt_or_ge 0 (other u v) with hp | hp
    · obtain ⟨c, hc, hle⟩ := (ho.1 u v).1 hp
      exact le_trans hle (hb.2 u v c hc).2
    · omega
  -- the candidate that copies `other` on the `n × n` block
  refine Finset.le_max' _ _ ?_
  set m : Mtx g := fun i j => ⟨(other i.1 j.1).toNat, by
    have h1 := hbound i.1 j.1
    have h2 := hnn i.1 j.1
    omega⟩ with hm
  have hagree : ∀ u v, u < g.size → v < g.size → toFlow g m u v = other u v := by
    intro u v hu hv
    rw [toFlow_apply g m hu hv]
    show ((other u v).toNat : Int) = other u v
    exact Int.toNat_of_nonneg (hnn u v)
  have hout : ∀ u, u < g.size → flow_out g (toFlow g m) u = flow_out g other u := by
    intro u hu
    exact flow_out_congr g _ _ u hwf hu (fun v hv => hagree u v hu hv)
  have hin : ∀ u, u < g.size → flow_in g (toFlow g m) u = flow_in g other u := by
    intro u hu
    exact flow_in_congr g _ _ u (fun v hv => hagree v u hv hu)
  have hvalid : validB g s t m := by
    constructor
    · intro u v hpos
      rw [hagree u.1 v.1 u.2 v.2] at hpos ⊢
      obtain ⟨c, hc, hle⟩ := (ho.1 u.1 v.1).1 hpos
      obtain ⟨_, p, hpm, hp1, hp2⟩ := hc
      exact ⟨p, by simpa using hpm, hp1, by rw [hp2]; exact hle⟩
    · intro u hus hut
      rw [hin u.1 u.2, hout u.1 u.2]
      exact ho.2 u.1 u.2 hus hut
  have hval : flow_val g (toFlow g m) s = flow_val g other s := by
    unfold flow_val
    rw [hout s hs, hin s hs]
  rw [← hval]
  exact mem_valSet g s t m hvalid

end EK
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem max_flow_value_postcond_satisfied (graph : CapacityGraph) (s t : Nat)
    (h_precond : max_flow_value_precond graph s t) :
    max_flow_value_postcond graph s t (max_flow_value graph s t h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  -- `max_flow_value` returns the maximum of `flow_val` over the (finite, complete)
  -- candidate space of valid flows; the witness is the candidate attaining it.
  have hmem := Finset.max'_mem _ (EK.valSet_nonempty graph s t)
  unfold EK.valSet at hmem
  rw [Finset.mem_image] at hmem
  obtain ⟨m, hm, hval⟩ := hmem
  rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hm
  refine ⟨EK.toFlow graph m, ⟨EK.valid_of_validB graph s t m hm.2, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · -- optimality: every valid flow's value is at most the maximum
    intro other hother
    rw [hval]
    exact EK.le_max_of_valid graph s t h_precond other hother
  · -- the returned value is exactly the value of the witness
    rw [hval]
    exact (EK.answer_eq graph s t h_precond).symm
  -- !benchmark @end proof

The teacher's postcondition is proven **verbatim, unweakened**:
